articleTitle: COVID-19 and GCC Islamic market Indices
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The study aims to analyze the impact of COVID-19 pandemic on the GCC Islamic market indices by taking daily prices of stock market indices from SP Global website during the period from 4th June 2019 to 4th July 2020. The study argues that the Dow Jones Islamic indices tend to follow the most conservative screening process, among other Islamic indices, which will allow us to have a clear comparison between them and the conventional counterpart. The study utilized three risk-adjusted performance measures including Sharpe ratio, Treynor ratio and Jensen alpha which are calculated pre- and during COVID-19 period. The study concludes that Islamic indices have outperformed the conventional indices during the COVID-19 period. The findings of the study indicate that the risk profile of the Islamic market indices is low as compared to the conventional indices. The findings of the study are expected to help the investors in better designing their portfolio.

articleTitle: Is There A Link Between Increasing The Degree Of Economic Freedom And Energy Consumption?
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The four main factors of financial development, EF, GDP, and gasoline pricing on the effect of gasoline demand, are investigated in the countries with the highest economic freedom (EF). Panel data from 1996 to 2017 were tested using the ARDL panel method. This study found some interesting results by testing four assumptions. According to the results, the price of gasoline and financial development have an important influence in reducing gasoline use. Moreover, EF and GDP are directly related to increased energy use. Whereas the financial crises (dummy variable) have an important original association with energy use. Finally, the Dumitrescu and Hurlin causality test was used to generate the results, which can aid policymakers in making better decisions.

articleTitle: The Impact of Occupational Stress and Burnout Among Employees of Different Age Groups on Job Satisfaction: Evidence from Saudi Arabia and Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to investigate the effects that occupational stress and symptoms of burnout have on employees of different age groups and analyze the impact of occupational stress, symptoms of burnout, and age on the perceived job satisfaction of the employees. This research has adopted a quantitative research method that included a survey of employees in two different age groups: younger employees (40 years old and below) and older employees (41 years old and above). SPSS is the software used to analyze the survey data. The result showed that there are significant differences in the emotional symptoms of burnout between the younger and older employees. However, no significant differences were found between the two age groups for occupational stress, physical symptoms of burnout, and behavioral symptoms of burnout. Results also showed that both occupational stress and emotional symptoms of burnout have a significant effect on the employees' job satisfaction, whereas age, behavioral symptoms of burnout, and physical symptoms of burnout were found to have no effect on job satisfaction.

articleTitle: Opening Qard Hasan accounts as sources and uses of funds and its effects on the market share of Islamic banks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The objective of this study is to explore how the opening of Qard Hasan accounts as major sources and uses of funds will positively contribute to increase the market share of Islamic banks. The study is based on purely theoretical multiple regression model where partial derivatives are applied to evaluate the effects of individual variables. The findings suggest that if the Islamic Banks adopt the policy of opening Qard Hasan accounts both for lending and borrowing purposes, it will attract more customers and channel more funds into the Islamic banks and as a result, the market share of the Islamic Banks will increase. If Islamic banks pursue the policy of opening Qard Hasan accounts in massive scale, it will also increase the monetization ratio which in turn, will increase market share of the Islamic Banks. Finally, Qard Hasan funds will attract multitudes of customers and increase in Qard Hasan loans in the economy will increase the money supply which will cause a rightward shift in the aggregate demand curve and as a result, both real GDP and employment level will increase, and unemployment rate will fall. Consequently, such prosperity will help people to open more accounts and deposit more funds and as a result, the market share of the Islamic banks will increase. This study is one of the latest attempts to evaluate the effects of opening Qard Hasan accounts in massive scale in all Islamic banks and how it will impact on the market share of Islamic banks. This study will be immensely useful to Islamic banks, Central bank, policy makers, People who are under the poverty line, research scholars, students, and academicians across the world.

articleTitle: Investing in value added production process as well as in working capital, and making Murabaha more effective, competitive, and lowest cost for the Customers of Islamic banks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The objective of this study is to analyze why the current Murabaha pricing of Islamic banks is inefficient, expensive, and least competitive compared to new Murabaha price suggested in this study. This study is based on a theoretical mathematical model where a few theorems have been established about the new Murabaha pricing and the inefficiency of current Murabaha pricing. The study suggests that the new Murabaha pricing for Islamic banks is efficient, competitive, and cheaper for the customers and it is expected that the market share of Islamic banks will expand rapidly. If the Islamic banks adopt the new Murabaha pricing as developed in this study, more and more customers will join and the manufacturing sector, as well as the real economy will grow which in turn, will increase real GDP, employment, and prosperity of the economy. This study will be immensely useful to Islamic bankers, Shariah Scholars, Central Bank, Governments, policy makers, research scholars, students, and academicians across the world.

articleTitle: The Influence of Islam in Work-Family Conflict and Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Currently there is a shift in the family model from the conventional family model where in the man as the breadwinner, to a dual income family model, where the wife also involves in supporting the family financially by joining the workforce. This study aims to explore work-family conflict that is associated with religiosity especially Islamic perspective, where the majority of the population of the study area is Muslim. The study of work-family conflict, hereinafter referred to as WFC, has such an important value because it confirms the relationship between work and family with job satisfaction, performance, depression levels, organizational support and many factors that trigger work-family conflicts that show a relationship between the two. This paper is expected to be a practical scientific revolution with the development of a broader theory for family work relations in areas where the majority of the population predominantly is Muslim. This research was conducted through a qualitative descriptive approach, which resulted in two propositions: (a) WFC will potentially reduce one's performance, (b) Religiosity potentially reduce tension of WFC.

articleTitle: The Nonparametric DEA Method for Portfolio Constructions in a Non-Islamic Stock Market: The Case of the US
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: We propose a novel approach to construct integral metrics for selection of stocks in a portfolio based on the nonparametric Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) method. For the period 2007–2020 and a non-Islamic stock market (the US), we evaluate and compare the return and the return-risk ratios for 110 different stock portfolios. We reveal that debt burden, the Price to Book multiplier, the ratio of the current price to the 52 week high price, and the stable growth of revenue and operating income significantly impact on stock returns of the US companies. The sectoral affiliation and the phase of business cycle are also significant. Our approach allows us to construct portfolios which significantly outperformed the S&P 500 index in 2007–2020 by the total return, Sharpe and Treynor ratios and showed a positive Jensen's alpha.

articleTitle: The Influence of Product and Price to Customer Satisfaction: Case Study at Sharia Compliant Hotel
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The halal industry is developing rapidly all over the world due to the development of the food industry that manufactures imported-taste food and other non-food industries, such as pharmacy, cosmetics, bath essentials, and medical devices. Whilst in service industries, it is due to the existence of many tourism objects that are served by halal tourism providers. Among others is the sharia-compliant hotel industry, in which the business providers will consider halal concept or Islamic law for all products, facilities, services, and prices. This research aims to identify the existence of positive and significant value between the independent variables, which are product and price, towards the dependent variable, which is customer satisfaction, as well as to identify the level of relationship between a variable of product and price towards customer satisfaction. 40 questionnaire data are collected, and double linear regression analysis is performed by involving the F test (simultaneous significant test) and t-test (partial test). Based on the test or method, the result is generated, stated that variable of product and price has a positive and significant influence towards variable of customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Textual analysis of moral components in Islamic and Non-Islamic business in Russia
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: This article examines the possibility of improving financial modeling through the use of textual analysis methods, in particular, the analysis of the moral component of the texts to determine the attitude of people to the object of analysis. The data source for the analysis is proposed to be a large portal with reviews of Islamic and Non-Islamic business from the customers who describe their experience with the object of analysis. A way to study social assessments of business models ethics in modern Russia based on an adaptation of the dictionary MFD was developed, the results showed the greatest coverage of the block “authority”.

articleTitle: Shura or Consultative Decision Making and its effectiveness in establishing unity, strength and commitment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to examine the effectiveness of Shura or Consultative decision making in establishing unity, strength and commitment for all the stakeholders. Shura or Consultative decision making has its roots in the Quran and in the Sunnah and it is one of the most effective way to make correct decision. This paper outlines how such Shura or Consultative decision-making process encourages the participation of others where everyone can contribute his or her expertise on any issue in correct decision making and at the same time, everyone feels that they belong to that institution. As a result, this Shura form of decision making unites the hearts and minds of the people and minimizes discord, infighting, and divisions. Shura or consultative decision-making process was practiced successfully and therefore, it is not just theoretical principle rather practical and applied discourse and has tremendous practical value in bringing unity, strength and commitment between the leader and the followers. This is not an imposed decision rather decisions emerge from the people through their Mashuara or consultation process. The consultation process itself is creative and unifying and brings the people together towards success and prosperity.

articleTitle: Sustainability Reporting by Sharia-Compliant Companies in Asia Pacific: Do Profitability and Corporate Governance Attributes Matter?
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The purpose of this research is to analyze the potential role of profitability and corporate governance (board independence and audit committee meeting) in sustainability reporting by sharia-compliant companies listed at FTSE Russell sharia compliant index. The samples of this study consist of 19 Leading Companies listed at FTSE Russell sharia compliant index in Asia Pacific from 2016- 2020. The total observation are 95 data containing of the annual and sustainability reports of the leading companies were examined using multiple linear regression. Interestingly, the findings show that the corporate governance (board independence and audit committee meeting), and profitability have no association with sustainability reporting disclosure. This finding may suggest the less effectiveness of corporate governance attributes in supporting the sustainability reporting. Additionally a good profitability may unlikely motivate the companies to report on sustainability.

articleTitle: Identifying Default Correlation via a Mix of Correlated Bernoulli Distributions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Default correlation presence imply higher credit losses. Its proper identification from empirical data is challenging. It turns out that the real-world data is a mixture of distributions, rather than a homogenous one. We show how to model it using a mixture of correlated Bernoulli ones. We show that the United States total loan loss statistics for the last 30 years is best proxied by a mix of 87% for a risk-free distribution and a 13% for the one with the default probability of 22 % and default correlation of +26%.

articleTitle: Reexamining the EKC Hypothesis in a Islamic Country: Evidence from Threshold Regression
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: This paper studies the existence of EKC theory in a Islamic country i.e. Islamic Republic of Pakistan in a nonlinear framework, by implementing novel endogenous threshold autoregressive (TAR) models for approximation and interpretation. The role of GDP per capita, energy consumption per capita, ratio of exports and imports to GDP(%) and net ODA received (% of GNI) in influencing the ecological footprint of production and consumption of Pakistan is analyzed in the context of EKC theory for the period 1965 to 2017. The research determine the nonlinear effects in the association among Economic growth and Ecological footprint from both production and consumption based approach. The results of estimated production and consumption based threshold regression model (TAR) indicate 713.65 USD as the threshold per capita income. The paper also established Pakistan has come to a turning point in the year 1988 and pursued by a diminishing pattern in environmental deterioration. In addition, the empirical findings confirm the presence of EKC theory in Pakistan.

articleTitle: A nexus between Exploration, Exploitation, Quality Ambidexterity, and Innovation Ambidexterity in Covid-19 pandemic: Exploring the moderating role of IT Ambidexterity
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The present study examines the nexus between exploration, exploitation, quality ambidexterity, and innovation ambidexterity in the Covid-19 pandemic through moderating role of IT Ambidexterity. The data were collected from the faculty and admin staff of universities of Pakistan through an online survey due to the Covid-19 situation. A total number of 280 valid questionnaires were received and utilized for the final analysis. The PLE-SEM technique was employed to analyze the current model. The empirical findings of the study reveal that exploration, quality ambidexterity, exploitation, and IT ambidexterity are significantly and positively associated with innovation ambidexterity. Moreover, the moderating role of IT ambidexterity was also significant between exploitation and innovation ambidexterity. Hence, this study's findings confirm that technology presence and advancement are integral for universities to conduct academic and admin functions.

articleTitle: Content Analysis of Halal Information on Product Website
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Businesses using e-commerce have experienced a sharp increase since the COVID-19 pandemic. The use of e-commerce has increased by five to ten times. The use of e-commerce for business transactions must be considered in purchasing, especially business transactions for purchasing products such as food and beverages. Because, in Islam itself, every Muslim must consume halal food. The purpose of this study is to determine the availability of halal information in e-commerce and find out what improvements can be made by e-commerce business actors. Data were obtained through the observations of e-commerce products. The method used in this research is descriptive analysis. From the results of the study, we know that the form of inclusion of halal information in e-commerce is currently in the form of halal information on product titles, halal labels on product photos, and halal information on product descriptions based on halal certification and statements of business actors. Furthermore, improvements that can be made by business actors are to pay more attention to halal information on the products they sell by providing product halal information. So it is concluded that based on observations on e-commerce, the existence of halal information is still limited.

articleTitle: Public Debt and Decentralization: A Sub National Evidence from a Non-Arab Muslim Federation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: A very few Muslim countries follow the system of federalism, whereas most of them are unitary states. The economic dynamics of non-Arab Muslim countries are different specifically in context of their reliance on debt, so as Pakistan. The rising government debt has now become an overarching theme in Pakistan's economic management, still a very attention is paid to public debt of provinces and their fiscal solvency. The debt is one of the chronic problems of Pakistan and it is attributable to persistent and high fiscal deficits, large non-development expenditures, weak debt repayment capacity, low tax-to-GDP, rising cost of domestic and external borrowing. The most significant structural roots of debt's are in low tax effort of successive governments. The problem of VFIs affect lead to accumulation of debt. Post Eighteenth Amendment to the Constitution in 2010, abolishment of concurrent list and devolution of few taxes to provinces has increased both provincial responsibilities and resource pool, yet state's fiscal performance is not at par. This warrants a need for an empirical framework to assess the persistent state of VFIs and the accumulation of debt. This study is an empirical model of public debt based on balanced panel data of sub-national (provincial) governments from 1971–2020 (fifty years), this is the first study in Pakistan to offer empirical examination of public debt in context of fiscal federalism and decentralization. Our Panel Corrected Standard Errors (PCSE) model suggests that VFI, expenditure decentralization and population density contribute to accumulation of debt [Hypothesis 1, 2 & 4] at sub-national level, whereas economic growth [Hypothesis-4] has corrective effect on public debt of provinces.

articleTitle: Issuing Credit cards on the basis of Musharaka and Qard Hasan and its effects on the earnings of the card holders
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The objective of this paper is to introduce Musharaka-Qard Hasan based credit card where both the issuer (Islamic Banks) and the card holders will share income from the credit card business and the issuer, or the Islamic bank will always offer Qard Hasan financing for the credit limit as well as on outstanding balance as part of the contribution to credit card business while card holder will make all the transactions and payments. The current study is based on theoretical mathematical and multiple regression model where partial derivatives are used to examine the effects of each of the independent variable. The findings suggest that the Musharaka-Qard Hasan based credit card will eliminate doubtful (Shubuhat) modes of financing currently embedded in most of the credit cards issued by various Islamic Banks. This is the first-time credit card based on Musharaka and Qard Hasan will generate income not only for the Islamic Banks but also for the card holders and this will guarantee the shared prosperity promised by Islamic finance. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time Musharaka-Qard Hasan based credit card is to be introduced as a new and unique credit card in the history of Islamic finance. In this unique credit card, both the card holders and card Issuer will reap the benefits and will work as partners. It is expected that this new Musharaka-Qard Hasan based credit card will sweep away all other exploitative credit cards in the world and thus the market share of the Islamic banks is expected to grow without bounds in the global marketplace.

articleTitle: Islamic Banks Disclosure Tone Prior and During COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: COVID-19 pandemic affects the global economic condition starting from the end of 2019. The narrative section of the firm's annual reports was found to have an association with a firm performance from the previous financial crisis. For that purpose, the current paper studied the changes in the Islamic reported tone prior to and during the COVID-19 period from DICTION 7.0 master tones: activity, optimism, certainty, realism, and commonality tones.

articleTitle: Whether Cryptocurrency is a threat or a revolution? An analysis from ESG perspective
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The authors make a fundamental initial effort to conduct a qualitative review on the digital financial revolution called 'Cryptocurrency’, mainly to provide a comprehensive discussion on whether Cryptocurrency is a threat to the Environmental, Social and Corporate Governance (ESG) investing goals? The study also aims to draw the current landscape and future landscape of Cryptocurrency in the global marketplace. The paper makes a qualitative review of the most recent and relevant articles on Cryptocurrency published using qualitative analysis. Key findings of the study reveals that Cryptocurrency is an exciting financial innovation, but it remains a financial experiment. Cryptocurrency fails the test of objectives of ESG investing. It is further concluded that the more and more production of Cryptocurrencies is not good for the environment, and it is a real threat to the ESG investment goals. The findings of the study will help the prospective and potential investors in better understanding of the Cryptocurrency as the long-term investment avenue in the global marketplace. Even though Cryptocurrency received overwhelming response in the last decade or so, the academic research on Cryptocurrency is still at the budding stage, primarily because the academic literature of financial technology is at the nascent stage. Therefore, the present study makes an honest attempt to fill this gap and provide a comprehensive analysis of Cryptocurrency in terms of ESG investment perspective.

articleTitle: A Mediated Moderated Analysis of Psychological Safety and Employee Empowerment between Sustainable Leadership and Sustainable Performance of SMEs
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Nowadays enterprises are highly concerned about their sustainability. Sustainability of SMEs in a developing country is highly dependent over the performance. Sustainable performance of SMEs in developing countries is highly linked with the satisfaction of stakeholders. Likewise for sustainable performance and catering of stakeholders can be made possible with the help of sustainable leadership. Therefore, the purpose of the current study Is to examine the mediating role of psychological safety among the relationship between sustainable leadership and sustainable performance of SMEs. Furthermore, considering the importance of employee empowerment which is considered as a major resource for employee performance this study further analyzed the moderating impact of employee empowerment. For this said objective data was gathered from owners and managers of 100 small and medium-sized manufacturing enterprises in operating in Lahore, Sialkot, Faisalabad, Karachi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, and Rawalpindi/Islamabad through cluster sampling. The data was gathered through surveys, and structural equation modeling was run to analyze the relationships. The findings revealed that sustainable leadership has a significant impact on psychological safety and sustainable performance of SMEs, whereas psychological safety showed an insignificant effect over sustainable performance of SMEs, but the mediating role of psychological safety was found to be significant. Likewise, employee empowerment direct influence sustainable performance and holds a significant moderating role. The findings of the research are significant for practitioners as well as academicians because it revealed that owners and managers should design strategies to encourage employee empowerment and to provide them psychological safety. The findings of the study are limited on the data collected from owners and managers without involving any other stakeholders. Therefore, in future researchers are guided to involve other stakeholders as well in the study.

articleTitle: New Paradigm of Behavioral Finance in Islamic Banks: the Role of Leadership to Facilitate Creative Behavior
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate the transformational leadership represented by its dimensions (Idealized Influence, Inspirational Motivation, Intellectual Stimulation, and Individualized Consideration) and its impact on the Islamic banks' creative behavior in the Kingdom of Bahrain. Since the study of Debondt & Thaler, (1985) that introduced evidence on the effect of the cognitive biases on the stocks mispricing due to over/under reactions by the investors after receiving market related information, the behavioral finance has been involved in other financial research areas. Hence, the research applied the descriptive-analytical method to answer the research questions and test its hypotheses. The research society included all employees of the Islamic banks in the Kingdom of Bahrain. Overall, 317 employees from the Islamic Banks in Bahrain responded. The analysis was conducted using multiple and simple leaner regression to test the hypotheses. The results indicated a statistically significant effect of transformational leadership on creative behavior. The research has led to some recommendations, including increasing and developing managers' practices for ideal impact as one of the dimensions of transformational leadership through developing future vision capabilities, overcoming self-interest, and acting in a typical way that motivates employees to emulate them. It is also necessary for Islamic Banks to adopt and implement transformational leadership and all its dimensions, supporting their employees' creative behavior and developing their creative abilities.

articleTitle: Post COVID-19 challenges for the sustainable entrepreneusrhip
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The Outbreak of Covid-19 pandemic has proved to be destructive at economic, social, and ecological ends across the globe. It has disrupted human life in an extremely adverse way. The pandemic aftermath is yet to be completely realised, yet the scale of economic, social, and ecological damage is unfathomable. The situation has elevated the responsibility on entrepreneurial ground to bring in solutions at the affected fronts and work towards sustainability. It is high time to realize the significance of sustainable entrepreneurship at the time when pandemic consequences are severe and still unfolding which will show in the times to come. Though the disruption caused by the pandemic is huge on everyone and everything, the study reveals that sustainable entrepreneurship has comparatively less effect of adversities of COVID-19 than the normal business. This study presents the need and significance of sustainable entrepreneurship to address the damages caused by COVID-19 pandemic.

articleTitle: A Study on Customer Loyalty, Customer Trust, and Market Orientation Towards Online Business in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: By comparing the change in participants' business knowledge and business acumen to that of traditional corporate training, online business simulations serve as a disruptive technology. Customer loyalty is earned due to the unique nature of services, which increases reliance on technology and customer involvement in service delivery. Customer trust helps to explain why customers are satisfied with their online purchases, where perceived value functions as a partial mediator for relationships with several competitors. As a result, market orientation can either mitigate or amplify the effect of organizational culture on performance outcomes. Unfortunately, there is a paucity of empirical evidence about the mediating impact of market orientation on the organizational culture-performance link. This study aimed to contribute to the body of knowledge regarding online users/customers in the context of online commerce. Additionally, it looks for possible solutions to increase consumer trust, make customers feel secure, and increase customer loyalty to the organization. Following identification, it is necessary to investigate the effects of these elements on internet enterprises. Thus, the purpose of this research is to ascertain the proportion of respondents who utilize the internet and the relationship between customer trust, customer loyalty, and market orientation toward online companies (E-business).

articleTitle: Small and Medium Enterprises & International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS): Evidence from Emerging Economy
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Harmonisation of accounting practices has taken centre stage globally providing users with meaningful information to make informed decisions across countries, corporations and even small and medium enterprises (SMEs). Only few studies have addressed the challenges and needs of financial reporting for SMEs, especially in emerging nation. This study aims to explore the challenges and opportunities in the implementation of IFRS for SMEs in the context of emerging economy. Data was collected through interviews with selected SMEs in Brunei. It is observed that the IFRS implementation was conducted similarly to other countries where mostly adopted through institutional intervention, regulatory guidance and compliance in managing the challenges faced by the respective SMEs.

articleTitle: Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development Goals in Bahrain
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Islamic finance can be one of the critical drivers for the successful implementation of SDGs by 2030. The core principles of Islamic finance align highly with the sustainable development goals, especially Zakat and awqaf and Sukuk, which profoundly support SDGs. Islamic finance is considered a viable source to fill the funding gap in achieving SDGs through social micro-financing. Green Sukuk and other similar innovative Islamic products that alleviate SDG achievement are gaining global attention. In this paper, we have presented an overview of the Islamic perspectives on SDGs, the interrelationship between Islamic finance and SDGs, and how Islamic finance can promote achieving SDGs in the Kingdom of Bahrain. As a global leader in Islamic finance, the Kingdom of Bahrain is highly committed to the global sustainable development trends and is highly poised to achieve the target by 2030.

articleTitle: Factor Analysis on the Customer Decision for Product Buying of Halal Corned Beef
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Developing era encourages the change in consumption trends. Recently, people prefer ready-to-cook foods (RTC) and ready-to-eat (RTE) types of food due to the practical reason, easiness, and quickly served. One of the fast-food products is meat-based products, corned beef one of them. Yet, the re-processing and various types of corned beef products alert people before performing product buying, particularly for Moslem society who are specifically ordered to consume halal foods. This research aims to discover the Indonesian people's concern on the purchasing determination for packed meat, in this case, corned beef by using the descriptive analysis method and Partial Least Square (PLS). Three exogenous variables are identified, which are product knowledge variable (X1), product quality (X2), and product attractiveness (X3), and one endogenous variable, which is buying decision variable (Y). It is notified that the biggest factor that influences the buying decision (Y) for corned beef is the product attractiveness variable (X3) with a significance value of 0.687. Halal corned beef (X1) influences the Y variable positively and significantly with the value of Y variable of 0.188.

articleTitle: Evaluating the 2013 Islamic Banking Regulation Capital Reform Implication for the Valuation of the Islamic Banks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The scope of research papers on the banking regulation reforms and its effect on conventional bank performance gave the authors the idea to consider Islamic banks in this light. Especially since in 2013 the Islamic Financial Services Board (IFSB) proposed the capital ratio for the Islamic banks. The paper employs the difference-in-differences model (DD) that allows to evaluate the treatment effect of the proposed IFSB regulation on the Islamic bank stock performance. The authors collected annual data on 25 Islamic banks (treatment group) and 41 conventional/mixed banks (control group) from 11 countries in the period of 2005–2020. The results reveal positive sign for the treatment effect. We interpret it that investors perceive the new regulation for the Islamic banks as a signal of increase in these banks' financial stability that much outpace the accompanying costs of higher capital requirements.

articleTitle: Government Bond Yields Dominant Determinants in Emerging Non-Islamic Markets: The Resource-Based Case of Brazil
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The purpose of our study is to identify the dominant determinants of public non-Islamic debt cost through analysis of nominal government bond yields denominated in local currency. The object is Brazilian government bonds of different maturity (from 1-year to 10-year). ARDL models allowed us to identify the lagged dependencies of the variables, and the Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) methodology allowed us to select the optimal models with dominant factors. We consider a whole range of Brazil local currency government bond yields by maturity and lagged impacts of influencing factors.

articleTitle: Labor Policy Implementation in Informal Sector during COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The informal economy is the set of diversified economic activities where workers have limited access to labor welfare services given by the state. The informal sector has a great capacity to resolve the increasing problem of unemployment, especially in developing countries. A persistent gap exists in the literature that arouses the interest of researchers to examine the policy implementation concerning important demographic variables of households. In this connection, the current research has been conducted to investigate the labor policy implementation in the informal sector of Pakistan using primary data taken from division Bahawalpur, Pakistan. The data was collected through face-to-face interviews of 240 individuals by using multi-stage random sampling, and the logit model was applied to analyze the data. Empirical results of the study showed positive and significant relationship among occupation of the respondent, age of respondent, number of adults in the household, relation with local governance, education of the respondent, the income of the household, male-female ratio, kind of house and average education of the household on labor policy implementation in the informal sector of Pakistan. However, there the two variables (age and loan) are statistically insignificant to labor policy implementation. In the light of empirical results, the current study suggested that the awareness and level of education help to proper implementation of labor policy in the informal sector which directly affects the well-being of the people. Furthermore, Government should provide interest-free loans at the micro level to enhance economic empowerment. This study will also be helpful to the policymaker to develop better policies for the implementation of labor policy in the informal sector of Pakistan, as the informal sector of Pakistan's economy represents the major share in the country's GDP.

articleTitle: Bahraini Female and Social Entrepreneurs Networking Behavior
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Research that investigates female entrepreneurs and their networking relationships has evolved greatly in the last twenty years. Nevertheless, little research on female entrepreneurship in Bahrain in general and fewer have focused explicitly on female entrepreneurs in their social networks. This paper examines the motives for Bahraini females to engage in social entrepreneurship and the main factors influencing the development of networks within social entrepreneurship. An exploratory research approach was employed. Data was gathered through 14 in-depth interviews with Bahraini female entrepreneurs. Thematic analysis was used to organize and interpret qualitative data. Participants have strongly emphasized “self-fulfillment” as a motive for engaging in social entrepreneurship, indicating a need to satisfy intrinsic needs. Data analysis revealed that religion is the main motive for Bahraini females to engage in social entrepreneurship, while other sub-themes revolve around religious beliefs like reciprocity. This demonstrates that religion's values and social values inspire females to engage in this type of initiative. The analysis shows interrelated themes regarding network development, which are mostly spin in the “national culture” orbit.

articleTitle: Microfinance and social behavior: an agent-based model for profit-loss sharing contracts
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: Traditional microfinance as a tool for poverty alle-viation is becoming increasingly controversial. In contrast, after the 2008 global financial crisis, islamic finance saw a great deal of development with its partnership and risk sharing based models being championed. Today, the real challenge lies in assessing the impact of microfinance in a complex economic and financial ecosystems where both conventional and islamic microfinance institutions cohabit and growing clients are interacting with each other within their financial ecosystems. This paper introduces an agent-based model with the aim of capturing and assessing the behavioral biases and agents' interactions in repayment behaviors and on the market dynamics following the implementation of Profit-Loss Sharing (PLS) contracts and Charity in microfinance. The paper is one of the first to follow the ODD protocol in order to describe an agent-based model in microfinance and islamic finance.

articleTitle: Price Features of the Singapore's Secondary Housing Market in the Islamic Region
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The Singaporean housing market is a non-standard one as most objects on it are public and have detailed information for analysis and are publicly available. This kind of housing does not fully belong to hosts, ownership rights are based on lease contracts for 100 years. Due to rapid development of Asian economies and the Singaporean economy in particular, investors from all over the world look at these real estate objects attentively. An analysis of the determinants of pricing in the secondary housing market in Singapore (in the Islamic region) will compare the benefits of Islamic housing finance and traditional finance. Current research is dedicated mostly to the secondary market, it throws light upon the lease age effect on the price of Singaporean flats in changing economic conditions. The study shows that the age significantly influences resale flat prices and that macroeconomic factors are also extremely important in the process of modelling.

Author Keywords: housing price in traditional and Islamic financial systems

articleTitle: Achieving Sustainable Development by Preserving Capital: Analytical Approach
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Sustainable Islamic Business and Finance
abstract: The current study aims to suggest a mechanism for achieving economic sustainability in Egypt while also considering the environmental consequences. The study's goal is to revise the traditional system of national accounts, which measures a country's economic performance and identifies all economic changes without accounting for environmental and social costs; as a result, the study introduces a national income account adjustment that assesses the depreciation values of depleted resources on the one hand, and the monetary values of environmental retreat on the other. The study employed descriptive and analytical approaches to evaluate both modern ideas of sustainable development and the Egyptian sustainable development plan. The study indicates that data on natural resources must be acquired in an effective and timely manner to execute the proposed strategy. Finally, the study concludes that adjusting national income accounts and calculating sustainable income on a global scale, particularly for developing countries, will have a significant impact on achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, and that it may lead to a review of national comparison criteria based on sustainable income rather than current income.
